input.hypothesis: The Strait of Hormuz closes to commercial tanker traffic

nodes.statement: The Strait of Hormuz closes to commercial tanker traffic for at least 7 consecutive days within the next 30 days (by 2025-07-15).
nodes.resolution: Closes if Lloyd's/UKMTO advisories suspend transit or insurers declare the strait uninsurable for tankers for 7+ days; verified via Reuters/UKMTO reports.
nodes.rationale: Reference class: 1980-88 Tanker War and 2019 tanker attacks never produced a full closure; partial disruption only. Iran's own crude exports transit Hormuz, making self-blockade costly. Base rate near 3% for a 30-day window absent a triggering kinetic event.
assumptions: Iran retains incentive to keep its own exports flowing
No full regional war within window
nodes.marketQuery: Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic closure 2025

nodes.statement: A kinetic strike on Iranian territory or Iranian nuclear/military sites occurs within the next 30 days.
nodes.resolution: Confirmed if state-attributed strikes on Iranian soil are reported by Reuters/AP with Iranian government acknowledgment or credible attribution.
nodes.rationale: 2024-25 reference class shows repeated Israeli/US strike episodes after nuclear program escalations. Negotiation breakdown raises probability; a deal suppresses it. 25% reflects ongoing elevated but episodic tempo.
analogs: June 2025 US/Israel strikes on nuclear sites
assumptions: Nuclear talks remain stalled or collapse
US does not impose ceasefire restraint

nodes.statement: Iran launches direct missile/drone retaliation against Israel or US assets within 14 days of a kinetic strike.
nodes.resolution: Confirmed by Iranian armed forces claim or widely reported launches intercepted over the region.
nodes.rationale: Conditional on a strike, Iran retaliated in April 2024 and October 2024 analogs; conditional rate ~70% given regime credibility stakes.

nodes.statement: Two or more commercial tankers are attacked or seized near Hormuz within 30 days.
nodes.resolution: UKMTO incident reports or insurer war-risk declarations citing attacks/seizures in the Strait/Gulf of Oman.
nodes.rationale: 2019 analog: limpet-mine campaign produced multiple incidents without closure. Elevated IRGC naval posturing plus strike-risk environment supports 15% base.
assumptions: Plausible deniability preferred over open closure
nodes.marketQuery: tanker attack Strait of Hormuz UKMTO 2025

nodes.statement: Iran mines or attempts to mine the Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes within 30 days.
nodes.resolution: Confirmed by US Navy statement or detected mines/USV sweeps reported by CENTCOM or UKMTO.
nodes.rationale: Mining is the classic closure mechanism (1980s) but crosses a US-stated red line triggering military response; historically Iran has threatened more than executed. 5% conditional on severe escalation.
nodes.marketQuery: Iran mines Strait of Hormuz navy 2025

nodes.name: Gulf war-risk insurance premium
nodes.rationale: 2019 analog saw premiums spike from ~0.125% to ~1%+; a strike campaign could push 3-5%. Drives tanker rates and rerouting decisions independent of physical closure.
assumptions: No total loss of Gulf coverage

nodes.name: Brent crude front-month
nodes.rationale: 2019 attacks moved Brent ~+15% in days; 2024-25 escalations added $5-10. A credible closure threat implies $90-110; partial disruption +$8-15. Baseline +12 with fat right tail.
assumptions: OPEC spare capacity ~3-4mbd cushions partial loss

nodes.name: USO (W&T Offshore proxy: US Oil Fund)
nodes.rationale: USO tracks WTI futures; historically amplifies Brent spikes ~1:1 with roll-yield drag. +10% baseline on Hormuz scare, +25-40% in true closure scenario.
assumptions: Contango drag limits upside vs spot

nodes.statement: US-led naval escort/convoy operations for Gulf tankers are announced within 14 days of an escalation incident.
nodes.resolution: CENTCOM or Pentagon announcement of combined maritime security operations.
nodes.rationale: 1987 Earnest Will and 2019 Operation Sentinel analogs: US responds to Gulf threats with escorts within days-to-weeks. Conditional on attacks, ~55% given existing 5th Fleet presence.
nodes.marketQuery: US Navy escort tanker convoy Persian Gulf 2025

nodes.statement: A US-Iran interim nuclear/de-escalation agreement is announced within 30 days.
nodes.resolution: Joint statement or verified framework signed by both governments reported by Reuters/AP.
nodes.rationale: Both sides have shown appetite for interim deals (2023 prisoner swap template); escalation paradoxically accelerates diplomacy. 15% base; acts as the key inhibitor on closure.
assumptions: Israel does not veto via strike

nodes.statement: Major tanker operators suspend or reroute Hormuz transits for at least 72 hours within 30 days.
nodes.resolution: Ship-tracking (Kpler/MarineTraffic) shows >50% drop in daily transits vs 30-day average for 3+ days.
nodes.rationale: Operators pause on war-risk spikes before states do; 2019 analog saw brief pauses. This is the practical precursor to 'closure' even without physical blockade.
nodes.marketQuery: tanker transits Strait of Hormuz suspended 2025

nodes.statement: Saudi/UAE bypass pipelines run above 80% of nameplate capacity within 14 days of any transit disruption.
nodes.resolution: JODI/Reuters flow data showing East-West and ADCO pipeline utilization surge.
nodes.rationale: Combined ~5.5mbd bypass capacity; 2019 attacks pushed utilization up. Partial offset to closure impact, capping price upside.
nodes.marketQuery: Saudi East-West pipeline crude bypass capacity 2025

edges.mechanism: Regime credibility demands direct response to strikes on sovereign territory
Escalation environment licenses IRGC deniable naval action
Retaliatory campaign extends to Gulf shipping as asymmetric pressure point
assumptions: Shipping targeted as US-adjacent soft target

edges.mechanism: Escalation ladder: attacks fail to coerce, mining raises stakes
War-risk repricing and crew safety drive operator pauses
Mined lanes force transit suspension pending minesweeping (weeks-scale)
Operator de facto suspension constitutes functional closure even without blockade
INHIBITOR: escorted convoys restore transit confidence and keep lanes open
assumptions: Escort capacity sufficient for major operators
Escorts not drawn into wider war

edges.mechanism: INHIBITOR: de-escalation removes coercion motive for shipping disruption
COUNTER-FORCE: diplomacy suppresses strike probability
COUNTER-FORCE: escalation shock accelerates back-channel diplomacy
Underwriters reprice Gulf hull/war risk per incident
Insurance and freight costs pass into delivered crude prices; supply-risk premium
~17-20mbd transit at risk; even threat of closure adds large risk premium
USO tracks WTI futures ~1:1 with roll drag
INHIBITOR: bypass pipelines cap effective supply loss, muting price spike
INHIBITOR: escorts reassure operators, reversing suspensions

summary.headline: Full 30-day Hormuz closure remains a ~3% tail; the tradeable path runs through strike→retaliation→tanker attacks→war-risk spike→Brent/USO, with US escorts and a possible US-Iran deal as the dominant inhibitors.
summary.mainUncertainty: Whether escalation from a kinetic strike stays at the 2019-style deniable-attack level or crosses the mining/closure red line; operator behavior under war-risk repricing is the swing variable.
followUps: Track UKMTO incident reports and war-risk premium quotes weekly
Monitor US-Iran back-channel (Oman/Qatar) for interim-deal signals
Watch Saudi/UAE bypass pipeline utilization data as a price-cap indicator
Set USO stop discipline: closure tail justifies holding, but deal announcement implies sharp mean reversion
